data.name: Akhfash
data.gender_notes: Akhfash is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'khafatha', meaning to crush, strike, or overcome. In Islamic contexts, Akhfash can symbolize the power and strength of God, or the determination and resilience of the believer. The name Akhfash carries the meaning “Crushing, Striking” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Akhfash usually hope their child will grow to embody crushing, striking and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the overcoming of challenges and obstacles with God's help.
data.etymology: Akhfash belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Crushing, Striking.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Akhfash total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_english.name: Akhfash
in_english.meaning: Derived from Arabic root, signifying swiftness or lightness
in_english.long_meaning: The name Akhfash originates from the Arabic root 'f-kh-f-kh', implying swiftness, lightness, or flying. Historically, it was used for some companions of Prophet Muhammad. The name connotes a person who is agile, quick to respond, and dynamic in their actions. It reflects qualities of swiftness and lightness, whether in physical movement or spiritual responsiveness.

data.cultural_impact: In some Islamic folklore, Akhfash is the name of a powerful, celestial being, a jinn warrior, said to wield profound power to destroy and overcome evil. Stories depict him as riding a fearsome, celestial steed, bravely undertaking mighty tasks for the welfare of humanity and the glory of God.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Akhfash can be understood through an interpretation of the root 'khafatha'. As Muslims, it reflects our belief in God's infinite power and the importance of our reliance on Him when faced with challenges. It also signifies the internal strength and resilience a believer can cultivate through spiritual practices, allowing them to overcome hardships and strive towards success.
